primitives.name: Skill Translation Matrix
primitives.verbatim_quote: This paper examines this problem by analyzing which skills translate to the NBA game, dissecting what NBA executives value when selecting international players, and by analyzing which international statistics and characteristics are significant determinants of success in the NBA.
primitives.assumptions: Skills are quantifiable and transferable across leagues with varying competitive levels.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S_int ≠ S_nba, translation efficiency drops below threshold.

layer2.mapping: Maps cross-league skill compatibility via regression coefficients derived from historical draft data.
layer2.telemetry: Draft success rate and post-draft performance metrics

primitives.name: League Competitiveness Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: The influx of international players began at a low rate with players such as Drazen Petrovic and Vlade Divac successfully competing in the NBA in the early 1990s.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_i': 'League i competitiveness score (0–1 scale)', 'P_{ij}': "Player j's performance in league i (dimensionless)"}
primitives.assumptions: Each league has a measurable competitive baseline affecting player readiness.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When L_i < 0.3, player adaptation risk increases exponentially.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphically relates European league structures to NBA performance expectations.
layer2.telemetry: Player draft position vs. league ranking

primitives.name: Draft Selection Risk Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: The Houston Rockets picked Yao Ming with the first pick in 2002 while the Detroit Pistons selected Darko Milicic with the second pick in 2003.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_d': 'Draft risk index (0–1 scale)', 'D_p': 'Draft position (ordinal)', 'P_s': 'Player success probability (0–1 scale)'}
primitives.assumptions: Higher draft picks correlate with lower risk unless player profile mismatches.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R_d > 0.7 and D_p ≤ 5, selection failure likelihood exceeds 50%.

layer2.mapping: Quantifies risk of misjudging international talent based on draft order and historical outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Post-draft performance deviation from projected percentile ranks

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical structure emerges from the interplay between international player skill sets and NBA-specific performance metrics. A skill translation matrix models how attributes like ball-handling, shooting accuracy, and defensive positioning evolve under NBA rules and pace. The league competitiveness index assigns weights to different European leagues based on historical performance data of players from those leagues. Draft selection risk models incorporate both positional value and risk-adjusted projections derived from prior draft outcomes. These primitives form a dual framework: one for predictive modeling (GSI) and another for dynamic decision-making (GSE). Failure modes include overfitting to past data, ignoring cultural or physiological adaptation factors, and misalignment between scouting criteria and actual performance. The system must account for non-stationarity in player development curves and evolving league standards.
